title: Tips and workflows for Claude Code, Blender and game engine?
author: tomayt0
selftext:
Howdy,

I am a software engineer but a complete noob at game dev. 

Currently I am working on a tactical FPS game that is inspired by the old shooters like Rainbow Six and Ghost Recon (not the more modern ones).

I am using JMonkeyEngine for the game itself which is working quite well. 

However my main struggle is building maps, so I have gone for the following approach.

Claude --> Blender MCP --> Build Map --> Import into JMonkey Engine

This is the result, which is ok for testing the game out

[Image 1](https://photos.fife.usercontent.google.com/pw/AP1GczN-WPOe12R-ai8xq5WU8uND5Go5VXY0QEYBrJrzuI3ivsEmb6N-45nkIA=w2570-h1278-s-no?authuser=0)

[Image 2](https://photos.fife.usercontent.google.com/pw/AP1GczN-WPOe12R-ai8xq5WU8uND5Go5VXY0QEYBrJrzuI3ivsEmb6N-45nkIA=w2570-h1278-s-no?authuser=0)

I am interested to know how I can refine it more and shape it up?

- Do I need to get assets from Sketchfab or let Claude craft them?

- Should I download loads of textures so that Claude can paint buildings with them?

- For props and other game entities, is it better to have them added after the Blender workflow in the specific game engine?

tl;dr what is the boundary of Blender for making maps, do I just get the basics with it in Claude and then polish it in my game engine, or do I get it 90% done in Blender with Claude and then final 10% in the game engine?

If anyone has any skills or stuff to share, it would be appreciated

comments.author: esgoto
comments.body: Post the images in the thread, not in links
